R072-01.notes: Main idea is the swimming lessons; A/C/D are minor details or unsupported.

R072-02.notes: Para 1: dry inland town, cattle tank only water, 'moment for learning seemed to have passed.' B (afraid of tank) unsupported; C busy-job not stated.

R072-03.notes: Excuses refuted (82 degrees, swimsuit under dress), pause, then Tess asks if she can swim; avoidance is clear. B contradicted by her wearing it.

R072-04.notes: Relief 'as if... someone had finally offered to take one handle' = burden eased by sharing. B over-reads 'take one handle'; D contradicts relief.

R072-05.notes: Playful encouragement; Marisol answers in kind ('You'd be surprised'). A too harsh; D contradicts 'I could teach you.'

R072-06.notes: Directly stated. B contradicted ('Tess did not push'); C says shallow end/wall, not deep end; D unsupported.

R072-07.notes: 'the kind of thing people said to five-year-olds, but she noticed that it worked anyway.' Direct paraphrase.

R072-08.notes: Chin high + crossing a busy street = careful, alert, determined; paired with 'slowly' and 'not graceful.' B tempting (chin held high can read as pride) but 'to show off for the children' fails: the width-swim is at end of August, before the children appear. A contradicted by 'slowly.'

R072-09.notes: Para 2 question precedes bubbles (para 4) and final-Saturday events (para 5).

R072-10.notes: She arrived early before the class; 'never late... not about to start now' extends punctuality pride to her new achievement. B/C unsupported; D she accepts the teasing jokingly rather than disputing it.

R072-11.notes: Survey of unihemispheric sleepers plus closing paragraph on what they suggest. A/B/D unsupported or off-topic.

R072-12.notes: Directly stated. C borrows fur-seal detail; D contradicts. Fact check: accurate (open eye is contralateral, i.e., connected to the waking hemisphere; dolphins keep swimming/surfacing).

R072-13.notes: Directly stated. C 'never' overstates 'more often'; B reverses the eye direction. Fact check: Rattenborg et al. 1999 (Nature) matches: end ducks increased unihemispheric sleep and directed open eye away from the group.

R072-14.notes: 'toward the direction from which a predator would most likely approach.' Others unsupported.

R072-15.notes: Directly stated. Fact check: accurate; fur seals at sea show mostly asymmetric SWS while paddling with one flipper. 'Sleep with both halves... on land' is a slight simplification (some asymmetric SWS on land too) but remains acceptably accurate as 'predominantly bilateral'.

R072-16.notes: Para 3 topic sentence states it nearly verbatim; possible mild giveaway via topic sentence but that is standard ACT function-question design.

R072-17.notes: ~40 min/day in flight vs >12 h/day on land. Fact check: Rattenborg et al. 2016 (Nature Communications) reported ~42 min/day aloft and >12 h/day on land; accurate.

R072-18.notes: 'brief bursts... sometimes with one half... sometimes with both.' C 'never with both' is trap. Fact check: accurate (bursts of seconds, both uni- and bihemispheric SWS). Weeks aloft also accurate (tracking shows up to ~2 months).

R072-19.notes: Last sentence: 'no one knows how the birds manage on so little sleep.' B was answered by 2016 study; A/D answered in passage.

R072-20.notes: 'most dramatic example' = most striking/remarkable. A 'theatrical' is the common-meaning trap; D 'sudden' doesn't fit an example.
